content.comment_body: I am working with several [product_name] controllers configured in a network, including a panel display. I need a reliable method to detect when any of the remote controllers have lost power, since the network inputs on the master remain in their last state when that happens.

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. In your setup, the master/slave configuration with [product_name] works differently from what you might expect. I’d recommend configuring all devices as masters and using a client/server approach. With this, you can designate one controller as the central master and monitor a communication status bit for each device. Network inputs can also serve as diagnostic indicators to help identify Ethernet errors.

Switching to a master-master configuration hasn’t solved the issue, as the local module’s network inputs remain high even when a remote controller is powered down. While the diagnostic input does indicate a communication error, it does not identify which remote device has been switched off.

That's correct: the situation is as you've described. You could implement a monitoring mechanism based on a heartbeat signal (life bit) to track connectivity. Would you like an example of how to set this up?
I’ll prepare an example and share it soon.

Thank you, your example helped me solve the problem. I ended up designing the remote module to send a regular pulse that continuously resets a timer on the master. If the timer isn’t reset, it times out, clearly indicating that the remote module is powered off.

analysis.insight_summary: The core issue discussed was how to reliably detect when a networked [product_name] controller is powered down, given that network inputs can remain in their previous states and available diagnostic functions may only indicate a general connectivity error without identifying the specific device. The successful approach involved implementing a heartbeat (pulse) mechanism so that a missed signal per remote device unambiguously signified power loss.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes for a clear, direct notification whenever any remote [product_name] controller becomes powered off or disconnected, specifying which device is affected instead of providing only a general communication error.
pain_keywords: cannot detect which module is off
